title.zh: 固定 N=64 Weideman 等离子体色散函数

summary: Evaluate the fixed N=64 rational Faddeeva approximation with a stable positive-imaginary-axis evaluation and the retained branch labels.

capability: Fixed N=64 Weideman plasma dispersion with representable imaginary-axis outputs
Evaluate the fixed N=64 rational Faddeeva approximation and its branch labels, using erfcx on the positive imaginary axis and rejecting nonfinite final w or Z.
operation: evaluate the fixed N=64 Weideman dispersion function
dimensionless complex z to approximate w(z), Z(z) and method flags
discovery.model: homogeneous Maxwellian plasma dispersion special function
discovery.boundary: finite representable arguments outside numerical poles of the rational approximation; positive pure-imaginary values use erfcx without intermediate exponential overflow, while both w and final Z must remain finite

identity.relation: dimensionless complex z to approximate w(z), Z(z) and method flags
identity.direction: dimensionless complex z to approximate w(z), Z(z) and method flags
identity.definition: Z(z)=i sqrt(pi) w(z), with N=64 Weideman FFT coefficients; w(i*y)=erfcx(y)=exp(y^2)*erfc(y) for y>0. The nonpositive imaginary-axis exp/erfc and nonzero-real-part reflection branches are unchanged.
identity.model: homogeneous Maxwellian plasma dispersion special function
identity.coordinates: complex argument plane; array axes belong to the caller
identity.boundary: finite representable arguments outside numerical poles of the rational approximation; positive pure-imaginary values use erfcx without intermediate exponential overflow, while both w and final Z must remain finite
assumptions: Input units and normalization follow the declared ports; no physical parameters are inferred.
Both w and the scaled Z must fit finite complex128; negative imaginary arguments can exceed this output range.

inputs.name: z
inputs.description: Values of the complex variable to evaluate. May be a scalar or a real or complex `array_like` of any shape; axis meaning is caller-defined and this operator does not interpret physical axes. Units: dimensionless (normalized phase velocity z = omega/(k*vt)). Elements must be finite (no `NaN`/`inf`). Pure-imaginary z=i*y uses erfcx(y) for y>0 and retains exp(y^2)*erfc(y) otherwise, with the unchanged erfc branch label. Nonzero-real-part negative-imaginary elements retain conjugate reflection. Both final w and Z must remain finite.
inputs.constraints: Elements must be finite (no `NaN`/`inf`); pure-imaginary positive values use erfcx, with no intermediate exponential range cutoff. Both final w and Z must be finite. Nonzero-real-part negative-imaginary elements retain conjugate reflection.

outputs.name: Z
outputs.description: Plasma dispersion function value Z(z)=1i*sqrt(pi)*w(z). Shape exactly matches `z` (a scalar input gives a 0-d array), complex-valued `ndarray` (complex128). Units: dimensionless. Validity constraint: numerically valid only when all `z` elements are finite and away from the expansion poles; real points with zero real part give purely imaginary results.
outputs.shape: same shape as z; scalar gives a zero-dimensional array
outputs.constraints: All z elements and both final w and Z must be finite, away from numerical expansion poles; pure-imaginary inputs give purely imaginary Z.

outputs.name: w
outputs.description: Faddeeva function w(z)=exp(-z^2)*erfc(-1i*z). Shape matches `z`; complex-valued `ndarray`. Units: dimensionless. Validity constraint: inputs with negative imaginary part and nonzero real part return the conjugated lower-half-plane value rather than the upper-half-plane analytic continuation.
outputs.shape: same shape as z; scalar gives a zero-dimensional array
outputs.constraints: Inputs with negative imaginary part and nonzero real part return the conjugated lower-half-plane value rather than the upper-half-plane analytic continuation.

outputs.name: method
outputs.description: Elementwise string label, `'erfc'` (real(z)==0) or `'rational'` (otherwise). Shape matches `z`; `object` array. Units: dimensionless (enumeration label). Validity constraint: must be one of these two strings.
outputs.shape: same shape as z; scalar gives a zero-dimensional array
outputs.constraints: Must be one of these two strings.

outputs.name: all_purely_imaginary
outputs.description: Boolean scalar; True means every `z` element satisfies real(z)==0, triggering the frozen source's early return. Units: dimensionless (boolean). Validity constraint: necessary and sufficient for `method` to be entirely `'erfc'`.
outputs.constraints: Necessary and sufficient for `method` to be entirely `'erfc'`.

preconditions: finite representable arguments outside numerical poles of the rational approximation
both final w and Z fit finite complex128; finite w alone does not guarantee a representable Z
supported: Evaluate the fixed N=64 rational Faddeeva approximation and its branch labels, including representable positive-imaginary-axis values via erfcx.
excluded: No mode identity or arbitrary-parameter accuracy is inferred beyond the declared numerical method.
Values with nonfinite final w or Z are not returned, including negative-imaginary-axis overflow.

failure_semantics.invalid_input: Raises ValueError for empty or nonfinite z; numeric conversion errors may propagate for unsupported Python objects.
failure_semantics.runtime_failure: Raises ValueError if either w or the final scaled Z is nonfinite. The existing floating-point warning policy and exception class are retained.
failure_semantics.nonconvergence: Not applicable; no iterative root solve is exposed.
failure_semantics.partial_results: No partial mapping is returned after an exception.

example.expected: The asserted result follows the declared output contract.

scope: Original N=64 source-method anchors and lazy imports; independent 90/140-digit imaginary-axis references at sampled finite values, including positive-axis overflow regressions, neighboring floats, extreme positive arguments, matrix shapes, and negative final-output overflow.
verification.evidence_ceiling: Independent references derive w(i*y) from the original erfc definition or its scaled positive-real integral at 90/140 digits, checking agreement before binary64 rounding. Sampled axis values compare w and Z independently at relative 3e-15, including subnormal outputs without an absolute-error floor; mixed complex values retain rtol=1e-12 and atol=1e-13. These bounded tests do not establish a continuous-domain N=64 error bound, arbitrary-complex-input accuracy, source-runtime parity or release approval.
known_limitations: Only the positive pure-imaginary evaluation is stabilized with erfcx. Nonpositive imaginary and ordinary complex branches retain their existing arithmetic; negative imaginary outputs can still exceed float64, and final Z representability is checked separately from w.
